# LiltKey

> LiltKey is a local, offline streaming voice typing tool for Linux and Fcitx5. Hold Ctrl+Alt to speak and release to finish; text appears at the cursor as you talk, with Chinese–English mixed dictation and automatic punctuation. Recognition runs on the local CPU and audio is never uploaded.
>
> LiltKey 是一款为 Linux Fcitx5 打造的本地离线语音输入法。按住 Ctrl+Alt 说话，松开结束，边说边在光标处输入，支持中英混合听写和停顿自动加标点。识别在本机 CPU 上完成，不上传录音。

- Product name: LiltKey. The package, command and config directory are named `fcitx5-voice` (config: `~/.config/fcitx5-voice/config.toml`).
- Current version: 0.4.0, distributed as a `.deb` for Ubuntu 26.04 (amd64), requires Fcitx5 5.1.19 or newer.
- License: original code is MIT; dependencies and pretrained models keep their own licenses.
- Runs on sherpa-onnx: a bilingual Chinese–English Streaming Zipformer model for default streaming recognition, a CT-Transformer model for punctuation, and SenseVoiceSmall for an optional offline preview mode. About 260 MiB of models are downloaded on first setup, after which dictation works offline.
- Ships a light Fcitx5 theme enabled on first setup; existing custom themes, dark preferences and fonts are preserved.
- The interface (status messages, notifications, setup prompts) and the docs are currently in Chinese only; dictation works in both Chinese and English.
- Existing pinyin input keeps working. Voice input is disabled in password and sensitive fields.
- Not provided: noise suppression, personal hotwords, cloud recognition, automatic rewriting. Accuracy has not yet been validated on a real-user dictation dataset.
